posts.name: Nielzabub
posts.cooked:
Trajector:

Mind control is a terrible plot element. The best (worst?) recent example is Agent Carter: the villain has the superpower of Being Able to Remove All Agency from a Protagonist, Until the Plot Decides to Release Control for Dramatic Effect.But it does make an appearance in Sentinels: Wrest the Mind.

I can't comment on the Agent Carter use, but all tropes are neither inherently good or bad for a story. It depends on how they're used. I'll agree with you that the most common use of mind control is horribly outdated in modern storytelling and does exactly what you described in robbing characters of agency until a convenient plot contrivance allows them to win.

 

I think the potential of Wrest the Mind is mind control done right. That three psychic damage backlash can be heinous, and it turns Wrest the Mind from a potentially broken card to something mechanically balanced that you only use when the situation is dire. The way I view it is that kind of psychic power takes a huge toll on Visionary, and so she only uses it in emergencies.

 

That would be how to do mind control correctly in a modern story. It has to have limits, and it has to have consequences for its use.

Silverleaf:

Finally I'm not sure how a "hero is forced to fall in love with villain" would manifest itself (in game terms) as anything other than a denial effect, for example not being able to attack the villain. And denial effects are boring.

 

  • Affected hero takes psychic damage when villain is damaged, damage would probably come from directly from hero. (Pained to see villain hurt.)

  • Affected hero retaliates against any target that damages the villain. (Takes vengeance against those that harm the villain)

  • Some variation on Miss Information's Isolated Hero, where the hero can't affect or be affected by other heroes. (Doesn't want to help fellow heroes any more)

  • The first damage to the villain each turn is redirected to the affected hero. (Jumps in front of villain to defend)

 

To be clear I agree with the rest of what you said, I just thought there were more ways to show "fall in love with villain" other than denial.
